text: US stocks fell sharply Monday as the AI and chip selloff deepened. The S&P 500 fell 1.9% to 7,418, the Nasdaq dropped 2.5% and the Dow lost 1.4%, based on preliminary closing data. Nvidia fell about 3.9% after its CEO resigned, and a new US rule restricting China's access to advanced AI chips added to the pressure, with Intel and Micron among the hardest hit. Investors are now watching Nvidia's earnings on Tuesday. The TSX closed at 35,722, down 1.1%. Globally, the STOXX 600 slipped 0.3% from a record, while Asia was hit hard, with Taiwan down about 6%, Korea down 3.6% and Japan down 2.4%.
mood: Risk-off: worry over AI and chip stocks, with Nvidia's results and export curbs in focus, spread from Asia to Wall Street.

veqt.t: Sharply lower: S&P 500 -1.9%, Nasdaq -2.5%, Dow -1.4%, led by chip stocks.
Down with global tech and miners: TSX -1.1% to 35,722.
Europe slipped off its record (STOXX 600 -0.3%, chip names and miners weak, healthcare firmer). Japan's Nikkei fell about 2.4%. FTSE, DAX and ASX 200 closes not found.
Tech-heavy markets sold off: Taiwan about -6%, Kospi -3.6%. Hang Seng rose 0.5%. Shanghai, Nifty not found.

label: Bearish today
